title: Resolve opaque player IDs in routes/memories.py and stop sending %20 display-name URLs

sections.what: Update all player-scoped endpoints in `routes/memories.py` to resolve by opaque player ID, node ID, registry key, or display name, and update frontend memory API callers to send opaque `player.id` instead of `%20`-encoded display names.
sections.why: `AGENTS.md` states "Node identity is an opaque ID. Display names are a resolution layer," and `engine/serialization.py` already publishes `player.id` (e.g. `0610fd64` for `sammy lopez`). Because `routes/memories.py` uses raw `app.world.players.get(name)` instead of `player_manager.get_player()`, `static/js/api.ts` and `commons-api.ts` are forced to send `/api/players/sammy%20lopez/memories/retrieve`, and any opaque-ID request returns 404.
sections.how: 1. Replace all 18 raw `app.world.players.get(name)` lookups in `routes/memories.py` with a shared helper calling `app.world.player_manager.get_player(name)` (matching `routes/graph_ops.py`'s `_resolve_player`, resolving registry key, `_players_by_id`, node ID, and display name).\n2. Update `static/js/api.ts` (`retrievePlayerMemories`, `reinforcePlayerMemories`, `getPlayerCognitiveMap`, etc.) and `static/js/commons/commons-api.ts` + `memory-context.ts` to resolve and pass the player's opaque `id` when present on loaded `worldState.data.players`, keeping `encodeURIComponent` fallback only when no opaque ID exists.
sections.verify: 1. Run pytest memory endpoint tests verifying `/api/players/<player_id>/memories/retrieve`, `/api/players/player_sammy_lopez/memories/retrieve`, and `/api/players/sammy%20lopez/memories/retrieve` all resolve to Sammy Lopez and return 200.\n2. Run JS unit tests for `ApiClient` / `memory-context` confirming requests use `player.id` when `worldState.data.players[charName].id` is populated, then rebuild TS (`npm run build:ts`).

acceptance.text: All 18 player-scoped endpoints in `routes/memories.py` resolve characters via `player_manager.get_player(name)` or shared `_resolve_player()` (supporting opaque `player.id`, `player_...` node ID, registry key, and display name).

Client callers in `static/js/api.ts` and `static/js/commons/commons-api.ts` prefer the character's opaque `player.id` when available instead of emitting URL-encoded spaces (`/api/players/sammy%20lopez/memories/...`).
Existing callers and tests that pass raw character names continue to resolve identically with zero regressions.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Mind / Memory Inspector views (`static/js/inspector/mind-view.ts`, `static/js/inspector/memory-view.ts`) and turn retrieval network calls triggered by `AgentEngine` / `MemoryContext`.

Current availability: Memory retrieve/reinforce/cognitive_map calls currently fire `/api/players/<encoded-name>/memories/...` from `static/js/api.ts` and `static/js/commons/commons-api.ts`.

Why no standalone new UI view: This fixes backend player lookup parity in `routes/memories.py` and client URL addressing.

Manual verification steps:
1. Load a multi-word character scenario (`Millwood.json`, character `sammy lopez` with `id: 0610fd64`) and trigger a turn or inspect Mind/Memory view.
   - expected: Network requests hit `/api/players/0610fd64/memories/retrieve` (no `%20`) and return HTTP 200 with scored memories; legacy `/api/players/sammy%20lopez/...` calls still return 200 for backwards compatibility.
